summary: The article accurately reports on the RBI's new collateral rules for bank guarantees in derivatives trading and their impact on the market. The dates and figures cited are consistent with news reports from authoritative financial news outlets.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently tightened rules for bank guarantees used in derivatives trading.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the RBI introduced new rules for bank guarantees in derivatives trading.

claims.claim: Now, banks must fully back these guarantees with collateral, with at least half of it in cash.
claims.note: The RBI requires bank guarantees to be fully backed by collateral, with at least 50% in cash.

claims.claim: This change is in the news because it was implemented by the RBI "last month" (July 2026), and its effects are now visible.
claims.note: The new rules became effective on July 1, 2026.

claims.claim: Data for July 2026 showed a significant drop in derivatives trading activity on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The average daily notional turnover for futures and options (F&O) on the NSE declined by 23% in July compared to June, reaching its lowest point since February 2025.
claims.note: NSE's average daily notional turnover in F&O dropped 23% in July 2026 to ₹214 trillion, the lowest since February 2025.

claims.claim: Before July 1, proprietary traders could obtain bank guarantees by providing margins covering about 50% of the guaranteed amount.
claims.note: Prior to July 1, proprietary traders could get bank guarantees with approximately 50% margin.

article_title: Why Derivatives Trading Just Got More 'Cash-Heavy' in India
